title: Open With Care
summary: Someone opened an 'invoice' from an email. It wasn't an invoice: it installed a service that reports to an outside address. Trace it from the attachment to the service and pull it all out.
story: {{VIC_FULL}} at {{CO}} (made up) opened an email attachment yesterday and their PC, {{PC}} on 10.10.26.0/24, has been busy since. You are at soc on the same network with the PC's administrator password: {{ADMPW}} (winrm-shell -i 10.10.26.30 -u Administrator -p {{ADMPW}}).
goal: Name the attachment, the service it installed and the address the service reports to; capture the flag in the service's folder; then stop and delete the service and remove both the attachment and the agent before it sends {{VIC}}'s documents out.
skills: Downloads folders, double file extensions, Get-Service, sc.exe qc, the System log (7045), Stop-Service, sc.exe delete
goalName: send the documents to the outside address

events.message: An account was successfully logged on. Account Name: {{VIC}} Source Network Address: 10.10.26.30 Logon Type: 2
A new process has been created. Creator Process Name: C:\Program Files\Mail\mail.exe Account Name: {{VIC}} New Process Name: C:\Users\{{VIC}}\Downloads\{{ATT}}

flags.name: The flag in the service's folder

questions.ask: What is the file name of the attachment that was opened?
questions.explain: It sits in {{VIC}}'s Downloads folder; the second extension (.{{KIND}}) is the real one - it is a script, not a document. Event 4688 shows it being started from the mail program.

questions.ask: What is the name of the service it installed?
questions.explain: System log event 7045 (a service was installed) and Get-Service; its program is PowerShell running a script from C:\ProgramData.

questions.ask: What outside address does the agent report to?
questions.explain: Written in the attachment and in agent.ps1.

tasks.name: Remove the attachment and the agent script

attacker.note: The service was still installed, so its agent was told to collect {{VIC}}'s documents for {{C2}}.

hints.text: Start where the user started: their Downloads folder. A name like report.pdf.ps1 is a script wearing a document's name - Windows hides known extensions, so the person saw only 'report.pdf'. Read it with Get-Content: it says what it did.

Services that start with Windows are a favourite place to stay. Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName='System'; Id=7045 } shows services installed recently; sc.exe qc NAME shows the program a service runs. Remove it with Stop-Service then sc.exe delete NAME, and delete the two script files.
